title: I had AI rebuild classic games with me as the main character. Bald head, blazer, rocket launcher. It took 3 days and I mostly just said "no, go DOWN the pipe"
author: Perfectz
selftext:
I now have 6 different games with me in it or reimagined, Mario with rapid fire weapons and bosses, Zelda with reimagine graphics and new abilities, Comix Zone as a instructional game that teaches me how to speak, Castle of the winds as a more true rogue like, Contra with me in it and upgraded to play more like contra hard corps, and I'm finishing up a variation of guardian heroes all running on my android phone.



How the Zelda sprites were made



Every animation starts as a video of me on a green screen, and a script cuts it into sprite frames. Zelda was harder than Mario, because NES Link is a chibi: a huge head on a tiny body, seen from above.



Step 1: Nail the proportions



Take Link's original sprites and upscale them as a proportion-only reference.

Feed that plus a picture of me into Nano Banana Pro (in Google Flow) to get a chibi turnaround: front, back and side.

The AI kept drifting back to normal human proportions, so a small script squashed everything below my neck to half height, and Nano Banana redrew it cleanly.

Step 2: Drafts in Google Veo



Use each turnaround pose as the start frame for an 8-second Veo 3.1 clip: walk down, walk up, walk sideways, sword stab, item get.

Every prompt ends the same way: "locked-off camera, character stays centered, walks IN PLACE like a treadmill, flat chroma-key green background, no floor, no shadows."

Use NES-style stabs, not swings. Veo loved swinging the sword around, and it took a very specific prompt to get a straight stab.

The drafts proved the look, but Veo decides the motion itself, so timing drifted between clips.



Step 3: Lock the motion in Blender



Rig a 3D chibi version of me and animate every move as a plain grey mannequin: walks, stabs, item get, hurt, death, even playing the recorder.

Use a fixed camera looking down at about 35 degrees, like a classic top-down Zelda sprite.

No props. The hands are empty fists, because the game draws the sword, shield, boomerang and so on at the hand positions. One set of animations works for every item.

Step 4: Restyle with Wan 3.0



Wan 3.0 reference-to-video takes the character image plus the Blender guide video.

Prompt: "Copy the grey mannequin in the reference video exactly: same motion, same timing, same camera. Flat green background."

It keeps the Blender motion and paints me over it, at about $0.08 per clip.

Step 5: Cut it into sprites



Extract the frames, key out the green, and line every animation up on the same ground line.

Record where the hands are on each frame, so the sword and shield sit in my fists.

TL;DR: Nano Banana for the chibi design, Veo for drafts, Blender for exact motion, Wan to make it look like me, and a script to turn it all into sprites.
